Subject: Service degradation: increasing tail latency

Hi Priyom —

We're seeing an elevated tail at Acme (us-east1) starting ~08:50 PDT. P95 looks OK (~120ms) but p99/p999 have spiked: p99 ~1.8s, p999 ~6.2s. Error rate up from 0.1% to ~1.6% (mostly 502/timeout). Throughput has dropped ~12% since the start.

Attached is a small trace bundle and a screenshot of the dashboard. Customer impact: checkout latency spikes on high-traffic pages. They are planning a marketing push in the afternoon — this needs a quick fix.

Attachments: p99_traces_20260618.zip, acme_error_snapshot.png

Can you triage and tell us whether this is queuing/backpressure (queue growth) or something in the model runtime?

— Marta Lopez

Quick triage notes (08:30–09:40 window):
- Observed sustained queue depth increase on acme's assigned shared pool (pool-us-east1-b) starting 08:47. Queued requests peaked at ~420 (baseline ~30).
- Per-tenant soft concurrency cap for Acme was at 64 and we saw sustained cap saturation for ~18 minutes. The per-pool scheduler applied backpressure (queue growth + increased scheduling delay) — not a model computation slowdown.
- KV/prefix cache hit rate dropped ~20% after a traffic burst; many requests missed cache and required full decode, increasing token-processing time.
- Autoscaler did not spin up extra workers because the pool had exhausted burst quota (burst_capacity_used=100%).

Immediate mitigation recommendations (can be executed now):
1) Temporarily raise Acme's soft concurrency cap from 64 -> 128 for us-east1 (safe for 1–4 hours).
2) Shift a subset of Acme traffic to the dedicated fallback pool (dedicated-acme-1) if quota allows.
3) Enable prefix/KV aggressive caching policy for Acme for the median 30m workload to reduce misses.
4) Deploy an emergency routing rule to route 20% of requests to the quantized-llama-q4 variant (latency tradeoff but reduces tokens/sec cost).

I'll prepare precise CLI commands and the script to revert caps. I also uploaded the p99 traces to the incident ticket.

— Markus Klein
Principal Infra SRE, Redwood Inference

Marta/Team —

Summary of actions taken (per your approval yesterday at 10:25 PDT):
- Increased soft concurrency cap for Acme in us-east1: 64 -> 128 (effective 10:30 PDT, automatic revert set for 14:30 PDT).
- Enabled 20% traffic routing to quantized-llama-q4 fallback model (reduction in tail CPU time observed).
- Turned on aggressive prefix/KV caching for Acme (cache TTL shortened to 90s for the workload window).

Immediate impact: p99 reduced from ~1.8s -> ~420ms within 14 minutes after changes; p999 reduced from ~6.2s -> ~1.9s. Error rate returned to ~0.15% after routing and cap increase. Throughput recovered to within 95% of baseline.

Next steps (short-term):
- Engineering to run a post-mortem on autoscaler burst handling + quota exhaustion and propose a fix to avoid near-term burst-cap exhaustion. Ticket: INF-9876.
- Product & Infra to evaluate safer automated fallback policies for customers hitting soft caps (policy engine tweak).
- CS: confirm credit issuance if metrics remain above threshold at 14:30 PDT.

I've uploaded the mitigation checklist and the final trace bundle to the incident ticket and Acme's shared folder.

Attachments: mitigation_checklist.md, p99_traces_20260618.zip

Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround. I'll post the post-incident notes to the runbook and schedule a short review with Acme next week.
